method: For each of the 105 sites in audit-sites.json, true_class was authored by reading source context before running Girder (see audit-sites-labeled.json's per-site rationale). Girder's actual per-site answer was then read via `girder analyze <crate> --json` (builds+saves the graph) followed by `girder inspect <graph>.aether --json` (dumps every node's raw call_evidence_v1 attribute), matching each sampled site's (file, line) against the CallClaim whose site.start_row falls within +/-2 rows of the sampled line.
not_a_call_site_finding: 53 of 105 (50%) of the sites this crude, Girder-independent regex sampler selected are not real call sites at all: match-arm enum patterns, generic bound declarations, function definitions, doc-comment prose, macro_rules! definition bodies, one block of commented-out code, and raw string literals whose text happens to contain call-like character sequences. This is published as an honest property of the sampling method itself (precommitted as 'crude but independent' before any site was read), not evidence about Girder. It also means the two shape categories most prone to false positives (operator_usage, fn_pointer_or_closure) contributed almost no real audit signal -- nearly all their matches were generic bounds or macro_rules! bodies respectively.

headline_finding: Zero unsound cells (0 overclaim, 0 unsafe_exclusion) across all 49 scorable real-world sites -- converges with the dispatch corpus's own zero-unsound result (32bd5d2) on hand-authored fixtures. Girder never overclaims certainty on real code either. But recall is 0%: every one of the 31 scorable must/may sites (28 must, 3 may) scored conservative (observed Unknown), and every single one carries the identical reason string 'rust-binding-or-dispatch-unproven'.
root_cause_confirmed: Traced to crates/aether-builder/src/mapper/claims.rs line 122: `function.filter(|f| f.kind() == "identifier")` -- the Must-proof eligibility check only ever considers calls whose callee expression is a bare identifier (a plain_call shape, e.g. target()). Method calls (receiver.method(), tree-sitter kind field_expression) and path/associated calls (Type::method(), tree-sitter kind scoped_identifier) are categorically excluded from Must certification by this filter, regardless of whether they are genuinely unambiguous -- e.g. gr.add_node(...) on a concrete Graph<...>, or UnGraph::from_edges(...) on a concrete type alias, both structurally provable as Must but never even attempted. This is a single, specific, more actionable root cause than the previously-named general 'same-file/top-level-only' and 'macro-argument' gaps (both still real and both also present in this audit's sites, but neither explains why EVERY must/may site failed with the exact same reason -- this filter does): on this sample, it is not cross-file calls or attribute-disqualified files causing the misses, it is that method/path calls were never eligible for Must in the first place, in-file or not.

next_action: The identifier-only filter at mapper/claims.rs:122 is the single highest-leverage next fix: extending Must-proof eligibility to method calls and path/associated calls where the receiver/type is a concrete, same-file, single-impl type would be expected to move a meaningful fraction of this audit's 31 conservative must/may cells to exact, without touching the already-correct 18 exact unknown cells (macro invocations stay Unknown regardless). Any such change must be re-verified against: this audit (re-run, expect fewer conservative/more exact, still 0 unsound), the dispatch corpus (32bd5d2, must stay 0 unsound and must_precision 1.000), and the Stage 1 trustworthiness oracle (f53f6dd, its union recall must not regress from 4/4).
